utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: Stela's.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the other room was used for storage. What kind of things were stored in this room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: Well, food and ammunition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the third room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: It was empty as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I think there was also a second floor. What was on the second floor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: There were three rooms again, and that is where we stayed. That is, we stayed -- we used two rooms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You refer to "we." To whom do you refer to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: The prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many prisoners were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: About eight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've stated that this building was the headquarters of Stela's unit, and you have been referring to Stela's unit as "Mrmak" and "Vinko Skrobo." Now, could you tell me, do you know any of the names of the soldiers who were members of this unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: I do, yes. Nino Pehar called Dolma, Ernest Takac, Semir Bosnjic called Sema, Buhovac nicknamed Hecko, and Dubi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the sake of the transcript, I want to make sure the names are spelled correctly. The second person you referred to, could you repeat that name and spell out his last name, please? It was Ernest Takac.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: Ernest Takac, called Brada, which means "beard."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The last person you've been referring to is Dubi. Is that a nickname, and would you remember his full name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: That is the nickname of the man called Dubravko Pehar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I see that it's spelled right. Now, did you ever speak with any of these persons you've been just mentioning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: Not directly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you learn their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: Why, I heard them while I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often would you see these people at Stela's headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: Almost daily.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of clothes would these people wear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: Well, depends. Some had multicolored ones, others had olive-green/grey.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they always have military uniforms on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: Well, I'd say yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have patches?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: I didn't see them at the time, only later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that later on you saw some patches. Could you describe the patch which they had on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: It was the emblem, a head and a sword through it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say it was the emblem. The emblem of what? Can you be a bit more specific, please? And was there anything written on the patch as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: Why, "Vinko Skrobo."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did the emblem look like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: Well, like that, like -- what do you call it? A shield.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit 51. Could that be placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, while they're looking for this Exhibit P51, could perhaps the record reflect whether this witness had observed this emblem before or after the end of January of 1994? Because the indictment ends at the end of January 1994 and he stayed until May. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Meek, don't you think it's too early to raise this issue at this moment? You have full opportunity to cross-examine this witness when your turn comes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I will never think it's too early to raise an issue, but I can wait.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You know, sometimes it's difficult for us to judge whether it's within the scope of the indictment or outside the scope of the indictment until we hear the complete story by the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, if you look at the screen. And if you want to see it more clearly, you can also look at the overhead projector. Do you recognise this photograph or picture?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does it reflect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: One can see the chequerboard, a head, and a sword through it, and the name "Vinko Skrobo."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is this the patch that you saw on the arms of the soldiers in Stela's unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you. That's it for the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: For the Judge's curiosity, can you tell her who is the man who is depicted on that? Who is the face that appears there?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Are you asking me this question or the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I'm asking you, Mr. Bos, and you can find out for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: We will find out for you, Your Honour. That's fine for the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you describe what your daily tasks were while you were staying at Stela's headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: Well, I went to the front line, fortified it, cleaned, washed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that you cleaned and washed. Where did you do this and what did you clean and wash?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: Well, mostly the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you say you also worked on the confrontation line. How often would you -- how often would you work there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: Well, when necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you give a rough estimate. Would that be every day or two or three times a week or once a month?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: Well, depends. Every three or four days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you asked to do this right after you were detained -- right after you arrived at Stela's headquarters? Was this straight after you were taken there that you had to work at the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: After two days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you say that you had to work at the confrontation line, could you be -- tell us a bit more in detail what type of things that you had to do.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: Well, I had to carry the bags, pile them up, dig, clean.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit 14.4. And I will ask the witness to make some demarcations on it, so I have here a clean copy if that suits. And if it could be put on the ELMO, again, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, take your time and look at this photograph and see if you can familiarise with what's on the photograph. Do you recognise what's on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: Well, I recognise a street. It's the Bulevar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, does this photograph -- can you indicate on this photograph where you usually had to work while you were working on the confrontation line? You should point on the photograph on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: Here, here, this building here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've said that you worked on several occasions at the confrontation line. Was it always in front of that building, or was it sometimes somewhere else as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: Well, mostly inside that building and behind it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask if the usher can give you a marker, and if you can mark the area where you would normally work. So make a circle around the area where you were usually assigned for your tasks at the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Witness, would you work there alone, or would there also be other prisoners working with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: There were others working there, too. I wasn't alone there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And whilst you were there, did you ever see any of the prisoners get wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And whilst you were there, did you ever see prisoners get beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: I did not see him being beaten, but I did see a man with bruises.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was at the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: Why, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is a very leading question. The Prosecutor testified by asking his question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with the Defence counsel. It is a leading question. You don't have to show him the locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I was just trying to clarify whether it was actually in that area, because -- well, I'll continue, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, whilst being at Tuta's headquarters -- sorry, whilst being at Stela's headquarters -- I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness KK, while being at Stela's headquarters, was there ever a time that an important person visited the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: Well, once one day when I was there, I was told -- we were told to go inside. We did. And I peeped through a window, and I saw a man with a grey beard, but that was only a glimpse I had. And later on, I heard from those others that it was Tuta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you approximately recall when this was, when this happened? A month would be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: The third perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean by "the third"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: March.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may ask which year, March of which year, for the record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could repeat what year it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you ever -- I'm looking at the clock. I have a few more questions, but they're not too many. So I don't know if I can try to finish my examination-in-chief or if we should stop it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you may proceed for a few minutes, but no longer than ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I think I can finish in ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You may resume.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, whilst you were in Stela's headquarters, did you ever witness any beatings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: Personally, I did not see -- personally, with my own eyes, I did not see anyone beaten, but I did see people with bruises.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your brother ever beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now -- and I'm going to ask you a question which may be a bit difficult, but if you say that you saw prisoners with bruises, could you say whether you saw these prisoners with bruises also before January 1994?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid that the witness is being asked to speculate and that is my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it's -- yes, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'd like to add that before that, one has to establish whether the witness can remember that time or not and then ask him to specify it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bos, you may proceed according to the directions given by the Defence counsel on this particular question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in the first few months of your detention, did you ever come across prisoners who had bruises?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you describe what kind of bruises these prisoners had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: Well, they were bruised on their heads, their bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you know the names of some of these prisoners who you saw who had bruises?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: I remember Asim Mustafic. Yes. He sticks in my memory best. And Edin Kasumacic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anyone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: I don't think any other name comes to my mind right now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you briefly explain what happened on the 25th of May, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honours, may it please the Trial Chamber, that is way, way outside of the scope of the indictment by four months, and we strongly object to this testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: First, there should be a division of the labour, as I've told you already. I see Mr. Krsnik was standing but you take his place. This is the first thing. The second thing is that according to Rule 93, that this Trial Chamber will hear any witnesses that are giving the evidence of a consistent pattern of the conduct related to serious violations of the international humanitarian law. We don't know what happened on that date, and we would like to hear it. It might be outside the scope of the indictment, but we have to know what happened on that day. When we evaluate the evidence in the later stage, we will take the full consideration of the objections offered by Mr. Meek. You may proceed, Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you explain what happened on the 25th of May, 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: On the 25th of May, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: My brother and I escaped then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you manage to escape?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: It was daytime, an ordinary day. We were in the garden of the cafe, about 4.00 or 5.00. There was some problems. There was a fight somewhere, and they all left. And we stayed behind, and -- the two of us, and we decided to flee. And that's how it happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a few more questions on -- you've mentioned a cafe. You said you were in the garden of the cafe. Which cafe was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: It was a coffee bar at the headquarters in which Stela was number one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that the coffee bar was at the headquarters. Do you mean was it in the building of the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: No, no, right next to that building, across the way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that Stela was number one in this cafe. What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: He was the boss, the owner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who would come and have drinks in this cafe?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: Soldiers, anyone who wanted would come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just one last question: Do you know the name of the street where Stela's house was situated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: It was called the Kalemova Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this cafe which was next to the building. Was that also situated on the same street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, I have to warn you, as I did with all other witnesses, please do not speak to anyone about your evidence until your testimony has been completed and do not let anybody speak to you about it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may, one small thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Because I think tomorrow morning, we examine another witness. And I think it may be good if the witness is informed of this, because otherwise, he may expect to come back first thing in the morning. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I will instruct the registrar to inform him about the schedule tomorrow, and the day after tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We are adjourned until 9.30 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
